category_title: Fourth-grade student with severe disabilities exhibiting physical aggression and escape behaviors
minimal_context: Joseph is expected to sit at his desk and participate in a reading activity while his classmates are present in the room.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Joseph, let's get started on our reading activity. Please sit at your desk and look at the book.

STUDENT: (Squeezes his fidget toy tightly, looking around the classroom and covering his ears) Too loud... I can't.

TUTOR: Just try your best to focus on the reading activity with the rest of the class.

STUDENT: (Throws the fidget toy on the floor, beginning to yell as his frustration grows) No! Too much!

TUTOR: Joseph, please lower your voice and stay in your seat.

STUDENT: (Screams loudly, pushes away from the desk, and runs toward the classroom door to escape, urinating on the floor as he tries to leave the room)

options.A: Employ positive reinforcement strategies during classroom activities, including verbal praise, tangible rewards, and extra privileges.
options.B: Show a short film about his experience with severe disabilities and communication difficulties, followed by a Q&A session.
options.C: Assign reflective journal entries in which the student is encouraged to write or draw freely on his experience.
options.D: Put couches into the classroom along with games, playing cards, and other artifacts typically found in a living room at home.
